headline: Comparable sales surge, margins expand, profit soars
summary_short: Five Below's net sales rose 32.5% y/y to $1,285.6M in the thirteen weeks ended May 2, 2026, driven by a 22.7% comparable-sales increase, while gross margin expanded roughly 380bp to 37.2% and net income more than doubled y/y to $123.1M ($2.21 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Net sales grew 32.5% y/y (down 25.6% q/q on normal post-holiday seasonality) to $1,285.6M, on a 22.7% comparable-sales increase — 18.5pts from more transactions, 3.5pts from higher average ticket — plus new-store sales. Gross margin expanded ~380bp y/y to 37.2% on lower store-occupancy and distribution costs, a lower shrinkage accrual, and lapping prior-year cost-optimization actions. SG&A fell ~290bp as a % of sales despite $51.3M higher dollars (store-support +$42.6M, incentive comp +$8.7M). Operating income rose to $154.2M and net income to $123.1M ($2.21 diluted EPS), aided by a lower 24.3% effective tax rate (vs 27.2% y/y). Cash plus short-term investments totaled $1,113.3M at quarter-end. Fiscal-2026 capex guided to $230-250M for ~150 net new stores; no revenue or EPS guidance given.
